title: But If Not: Daniel 3-4, Job 19, John 12, 2 John
summary: Daniel 3-4: the gold image on the plain of Dura (dated by the Greek versions to Nebuchadnezzar's eighteenth year, 587 B.C.) as the king's all-gold answer to the statue dream; the repeated lists of officials and instruments as the machinery of compulsion; 'we have no need to answer you' as a settled question (Calvin and Cyprian, paraphrased), the 'we can do more good alive' excuse (Calvin and Spurgeon No. 2217, paraphrased), and 'but if not' with Bryan Chapell quoted ('Our trust is in what God does, not what we want to happen'). The hard question was the fourth man, bar elahin, plural (Cambridge): Calvin an angel ('forced and frigid' otherwise), Hippolytus quoted (no name for the fourth), Jerome paraphrased (angel in history, picture of Christ), Gill quoted ('better... with Christ in the fiery furnace'), Poole's 'Angel of the covenant'; the host held the preincarnate-Christ reading with an open hand, anchored in Isaiah 43:2, with one NT move (Hebrews 11:34). Chapter 4 was taught as the king's proclamation with first person, third person during the madness, first person again at 'my reason returned'; the watcher ('ir, Theodoret paraphrased); 4:17 as the book's thesis; 4:27 'break off your sins' (Calvin over Jerome and Chrysostom's almsgiving reading); bricks stamped with his name (JFB); the Ligonier line 'a man who thought himself a god was made a beast' quoted; and the conversion question (Henry yes, Calvin reserved; host hopeful because 4:37 confesses his own pride). Job 19 covered the siege and abandonment, the inscription wish granted in Scripture (Barnes), go'el, 'stand upon the dust', and 'in my flesh' versus 'without my flesh' (Cambridge against Poole and Gill), with Clement of Rome quoted (1 Clement 26). John 12:37-50: Isaiah 53:1 and 6:10, 'they could not believe' answered by Augustine (paraphrased) and Chrysostom (quoted, 'because they will not, therefore they cannot'), Sproul's 'One Sent Me' quoted (Satan knows the truth but hates it) and paraphrased on judicial hardening, 12:41 Isaiah saw the Son, and secret believers who loved man's glory. 2 John: the elect lady (Clement of Alexandria's Electa, most read a church), truth five times, love as walking in commandments, deceivers denying Christ in the flesh, Irenaeus' story of John fleeing Cerinthus at the bath-house quoted, and Barnes and Ligonier on refusing endorsement rather than kindness. The closing connection was seeing: the king lifting his eyes, Job's eyes beholding God, Isaiah seeing his glory, and 'face to face'.
threads: Daniel 5-6 is next: Belshazzar's feast with the temple vessels, the writing on the wall (mene, mene, tekel, parsin), the fall of Babylon in 539 B.C. (Nabonidus and Belshazzar co-regency, the Nabonidus Chronicle), Darius the Mede, and the lions' den with Daniel praying toward Jerusalem. Daniel 5:18-21 has Daniel retell chapter 4 to Belshazzar, a natural link back. Calvin calcom24 continues (Lecture 23 onward, line ~11690 of the plain text); Jerome and Theodoret on sermonindex.net/commentary/ecf/DAN/5 and /6.

Unused Daniel 3-4 material: Calvin, 'for the sake of living, lose life itself' and 'we have already committed an atrocious insult against God, when we even question the propriety of swerving'; Spurgeon No. 2217, 'It is folly to be singular except when to be singular is to be right!'; Ligonier 'Courage Under Fire', 'they did not owe the Lord service because of what He could do for them but because He alone is God'; Theodoret, 'in his wish to snatch heaven he was driven also from earth' and the twelve months as 'the span of divine longsuffering'; Jerome on 4:34 (quoted only as paraphrase) and on 4:35 'like a worldling'; Henry, 'Nebuchadnezzar would be more than a man, but God justly makes him less than a man'; Irenaeus 4.20.11 lists the fourth man, the stone, and the Son of Man as appearances of the Word; the LXX Song of the Three Children insertion (Cambridge) was not mentioned.

Job 20 is next: Zophar's second speech on the short triumph of the wicked ('the exulting of the wicked is short', 20:5). Job's 'I know that my Redeemer lives' is now said and should be the lens for Zophar's reply. Unused Job 19: Ellicott's chain (daysman 9:33, witness 16:19, surety 17:3, goel 19:25); Gill, the words Job wanted engraved on his tombstone are 'I know that my Redeemer liveth'; Benson on letters cut in stone and filled with lead; Ligonier 'Job's Hope in the Resurrection', 'Job's vindication must occur even if he dies before it happens'; 19:28-29 warning to the friends not covered.

John 13:1-11 is next: the foot washing begins the upper room discourse (Book of Glory), 'having loved his own... he loved them to the end', Judas, Peter's refusal and 'If I do not wash you, you have no share with me'. Unused 12:37-50: Augustine Tractate 53, 'But if I am asked why they could not, I reply at once, because they would not' (paraphrased on air); Sproul 'One Sent Me' on missions ('there are no innocent natives anywhere'), and 'Isaiah saw Christ on the throne in His glory before Christ was even born'; Ligonier 'The Glory Isaiah Saw' quoting Augustine on hardening by withdrawing aid.

3 John is next: the elder to Gaius, Diotrephes 'who likes to put himself first', Demetrius, and supporting traveling teachers 'for the sake of the name', the positive mirror of 2 John 10-11. Correction to an earlier thread: Calvin wrote no commentary on 2 or 3 John (calcom45 has 1 John only), so do not attribute Calvin on 3 John. Unused 2 John: Irenaeus 1.16.3 ('not even to address to them the salutation of good-speed'); Gill, 'neither into the house of God... nor into your own house'; the Ligonier devotional's Machen illustration.

Voices quoted this episode: Bryan Chapell ('But If Not'), Hippolytus (Commentary on Daniel 3:26), John Gill (Daniel 3:25), Ligonier devotional 'God Humbles Nebuchadnezzar', Clement of Rome (1 Clement 26), John Chrysostom (Homily 68 on John), R. C. Sproul ('One Sent Me'), Irenaeus (Against Heresies 3.3.4). Paraphrased: Calvin (Daniel 3:16, 3:25, 4:27, 4:37), Spurgeon No. 2217, Cambridge Bible, Jerome, Poole, Theodoret, Henry, JFB, Barnes, Augustine Tractate 53, Clement of Alexandria, Ligonier 'Do Not Receive Him'. Desiring God still returns 403.

show_notes: Three men at a furnace say 'but if not', a fourth figure walks with them in the fire, and a proud king learns on all fours that the Most High rules. Job names his living Redeemer, John explains why the crowds could not believe, and Second John teaches love that guards the truth. With Hippolytus, Gill, Chapell, Clement of Rome, Chrysostom, Sproul, and Irenaeus.
